items.title: Stocks in news: Wipro, Lenskart, Tata Motors PV, Ather Energy and Kotak Bank
items.description: On Thursday, Indian markets faced downward pressure as they wrapped up trading lower amid mixed signals from global economies. Notably, Wipro's stock saw gains following its expanded partnership with Google Cloud aimed at enhancing AI implementation. Meanwhile, Lenskart's current investor is set to sell shares worth up to Rs 1,313 crore.

items.title: Close to clearing NSE IPO: Sebi Chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey
items.description: NSE's valuation in the unlisted market is around ₹5 lakh crore, potentially catapulting it to India's top-ten market capitalization leader-board on listing, based on current prices.

items.title: HDFC Bank's CEO call gains urgency as Sashidhar Jagdishan's term nears end
items.description: The timeline stands in contrast to Jagdishan's previous reappointment. HDFC Bank's board had recommended a fresh three-year term for him on March 4, 2023, nearly eight months before his first tenure was due to expire. The Reserve Bank of India approved the appointment in September that year.

items.title: Sebi proposes merchant banker exemption for small-value private debt issues
items.description: Sebi has proposed waiving mandatory merchant banker appointments for eligible listed issuers raising small-value debt privately. The move aims to cut costs and delays, while safeguards would restrict exemptions to regulated companies issuing senior secured debt rated AA- or higher.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
items.description: Indian equities ended sharply lower on Thursday as expiry-day volatility intensified after the first monthly expiry under the Closing Auction Session. Sensex fell 539 points and Nifty 117 points, while technical indicators signalled weakening momentum amid global and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Lenskart shares block deal: Alpha Wave Ventures II likely to sell 1.2% stake worth Rs 1,313 crore
items.description: Alpha Wave Ventures II plans to sell up to 20.8 million Lenskart shares worth ₹1,313 crore at ₹630 apiece, a 1.7% discount. The secondary transaction represents about 1.2% stake, with Lenskart receiving no proceeds from the sale.

items.title: Market wrap: TCS, Tech Mahindra, ICICI Bank, ITC top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.description: Indian equities rebounded on Friday, ending a two-session losing streak as heavyweight IT stocks led gains. Nifty rose 0.35% to 24,175.65, while Sensex gained 0.43% to 77,264.51. Analysts expect consolidation amid mixed global cues and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Where to invest as market headwinds ease: Motilal Oswal backs mid and smallcaps, favours gold over silver
items.description: Motilal Oswal says several headwinds facing Indian equities are easing, supported by stronger earnings, positive FII flows and domestic demand. It remains Neutral on equities but Overweight on mid- and small-caps, while preferring gold over silver and accrual-focused fixed-income strategies.

items.title: Retail investors bet big on these 12 smallcap stocks that rallied up to 150%; 3 turned multibaggers
items.description: Smallcap stocks are often associated with high risk and high reward, a trade-off that many retail investors appear willing to embrace. Shareholding data for the June 2026 quarter show that retail investors increased their holdings in nearly 124 smallcap stocks for the fourth consecutive quarter, through June ’26. The trend suggests growing confidence among individual investors. (Retail investors refer to resident individuals holding nominal share capital of up to Rs 2 lakh.)However, rising retail participation has not translated into broad-based gains in smallcap stocks. Performance has remained largely subdued over the past year, with only around 27 stocks delivering positive returns. Yet, even amid the broader weakness, a handful of small-cap stocks have emerged as standout performers. Here, we highlight nine small-cap stocks that have surged between 50% and 150% over the past year while also recording a consistent increase in retail investor ownership over the last four quarters. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: SBI General Insurance Q1 GDPI rises to Rs 3,506 crore; comprehensive income jumps 17%
items.description: SBI General Insurance reported 10.9% year-on-year GDPI growth to Rs 3,506 crore in Q1 FY27. Comprehensive income rose 17.4% to Rs 573 crore, while health, engineering and personal accident segments delivered strong growth, alongside a 2.0-times solvency ratio.

items.title: CAS chaos: How did Sensex crash 2,000 points in 6 minutes while Nifty stayed stable on monthly expiry?
items.description: Sensex plunged over 2,000 points during Thursday’s closing auction session before recovering some losses, while Nifty remained comparatively stable. Market experts attributed the sharp divergence largely to thin trading volumes on BSE. The episode has renewed scrutiny of the new CAS mechanism, particularly around monthly expiry and its impact on price discovery.

items.title: India can reach a $5.1 trillion economy by FY29 as growth strengthens: Omniscience Capital
items.description: India's economy could reach $5.1 trillion by FY29, according to OmniScience Capital. Stronger real growth and healthier balance sheets support this expansion. The pandemic and rupee depreciation had previously delayed this $5 trillion ambition. Real GDP growth averaged 7.4% between FY22 and FY26. An optimistic scenario projects India's GDP reaching $5.9 trillion by FY29.

items.title: HSBC initiates coverage on this recently listed healthcare stock that can rally up to 26%. Do you own?
items.description: HSBC has initiated coverage on recently listed Manipal Health with a Buy rating and Rs 1,000 target price, implying 26% upside. The brokerage sees strong growth potential from improving hospital utilisation, the Sahyadri turnaround, higher-margin speciality mix and deleveraging, with adjusted PAT expected to nearly triple by FY29.

items.title: Ola Electric shares rally over 5%, rebound 79% from March low. Here’s what’s driving the stock
items.description: Ola Electric shares rallied on Friday after the EV maker launched its new S1Z scooter range with indigenous Bharat Cell LFP technology. The stock has rebounded nearly 79% from its March low, while the new models target India’s mass-market EV segment with prices starting at Rs 79,999.

items.title: JM Financial calls Metropolis Healthcare ‘best-value diagnostic stock’, sees up to   27%  upside
items.description: JM Financial has retained its Buy rating on Metropolis Healthcare with a target price of Rs 734, implying 27.2% upside. The brokerage calls it the cheapest among India’s leading listed diagnostic players, citing attractive valuations, network expansion, stronger B2C growth and improving margins as key drivers.

items.title: Elara initiates coverage on Alkem, Eris, IPCA and Mankind. Check ratings and targets
items.description: Elara has initiated coverage on four pharmaceutical stocks, assigning Buy, Accumulate and Reduce ratings. Alkem Laboratories emerged as its top pick for margin recovery, while Eris Lifesciences and Mankind Pharma could benefit from portfolio expansion, acquisitions and deleveraging. Elara retained a cautious view on IPCA Laboratories after its recent rally.

items.title: Has the S&P 500 really doubled since 2023? Chris Wood says it is down 21% in gold terms
items.description: Jefferies’ Christopher Wood highlights a sharp divergence in market returns: while the S&P 500 has doubled in dollar terms since early 2023, it has fallen 21% relative to gold. He warns that efforts to suppress US bond yields could weaken the dollar, boosting alternative assets such as gold and Bitcoin.

items.title: Jefferies initiates SBI Funds Management coverage with Buy; sees 26% upside
items.description: Jefferies initiated coverage on SBI Funds Management with a Buy rating and a Rs 710 price target, implying 26% upside. The brokerage expects operating profit to grow at a 15% CAGR through FY29, supported by rising mutual fund assets, SBI’s distribution network and operating leverage. Strong B30 presence and lower operating costs further support the asset manager’s growth

items.title: 15 mainboard IPOs doubled investor money on listing day in last 6 years. See full list
items.description: It has been more than 20 months, or 609 days, since the mainboard segment of India’s IPO market last saw a stock deliver a listing-day gain of more than 100%. That long dry spell is finally over. Here are 15 stocks that doubled investor money on listing day.

items.title: Tempsens Instruments doubles IPO investors’ money as stock lists at 111% premium. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Tempsens Instruments made a blockbuster debut, listing at Rs 634 on the NSE, an 111% premium over its Rs 300 IPO price. The stock briefly gained further before falling over 8% from its debut level, though it remained 94% above the issue price. Analysts advised investors who missed the rally to consider buying on dips.

items.title: Sugar stocks rally continues: Balrampur Chini, Dhampur Sugar, Uttam Sugar Mills rally up to 4%. Two big triggers
items.description: Sugar stocks rallied as domestic sugar prices surged sharply over the past month. Government data showed retail prices rising from Rs 48.18/kg on July 20 to Rs 55.70/kg on August 20, with current prices around Rs 70/kg. Balrampur Chini Mills, Dhampur Sugar, Uttam Sugar, Triveni Engineering and EID Parry were among the key gainers.

items.title: HCLTech, TCS, Infosys, other IT stocks rally up to 5%. What lies ahead?
items.description: Indian IT stocks surged sharply, led by gains in largecap names, after Nvidia’s strong results and upbeat revenue outlook revived optimism around the global AI spending cycle. The rally came despite lingering concerns over AI disruption and mixed brokerage views on the sector.
